C-QUICKLOOK-SYNTAX-THEME.Summary: Make packaged QuickLook syntax-token colors follow its existing supported light/dark appearance by appending light-mode overrides to the existing github-dark.css resource, while keeping the renderer, markup pipeline, layout and the accepted QuickLook content boundary byte-for-byte unchanged.
C-QUICKLOOK-SYNTAX-THEME.Problem: Original finding DESIGN:F-007 is present in the current QuickLook sources. MarkdownRenderer.swift always embeds the packaged github-dark.css in both appearances, while style.css switches the document to a light background (light code-block background #f6f8fa) under prefers-color-scheme: light. markdown-it emits code elements with only language-* classes (no .hljs root), so nested hljs token spans keep GitHub Dark foregrounds on the light pre background. Source-bound Swift HTML evidence rendered in Chromium and WebKit measured highlighted string contrast on the light pre at 1.4438:1 versus 11.2542:1 in dark mode, with the unknown-language plain control readable at 14.8392:1. Current-state inspection confirms the renderer still loads github-dark.css, the resource still has no prefers-color-scheme branch, style.css still uses #f6f8fa, and the packaged highlight engine is 11.9.0. Native theme acceptance has never been executed.
C-QUICKLOOK-SYNTAX-THEME.Relationship: Bounded follow-up to the applied and archived C-QUICKLOOK-CONTENT-BOUNDARY; it modifies only palette declarations and verification on top of that accepted boundary and does not reopen any of its decisions. Originates from DESIGN:F-007 and the private reviews QUICKLOOK-THEME-REVIEW and QUICKLOOK-SYNTAX-THEME-SPEC-REVIEW. Those reviews cite historical baselines (main 0a72917c and a prior draft worktree citing 6989ef9e); neither SHA is normative here. This draft was composed against the current canary-beta-wave worktree; structurally verified anchors are listed in the constraints, and the plan must re-verify file digests and anchors on the fresh head before approval.

Goals.Goal: In the existing prefers-color-scheme: light branch, apply the specified light syntax palette to every color-bearing token group of the packaged highlight stylesheet (13 groups covering all 41 existing color-bearing selectors). Keep dark/default syntax appearance and all non-color rendering behavior unchanged.

Require at least 4.5:1 unrounded foreground/background contrast for every light code-token group, including addition/deletion measured against their own backgrounds rather than the pre background, and including inherited-foreground controls. This is a bounded code-readability criterion, not a claim of overall WCAG conformance.

Prove the palette on the actual Swift-produced Markdown/highlight pipeline in Chromium and WebKit, and on the actual PreviewProvider/WKWebView native fixture under isolated light and dark appearances, with fail-closed result validation. Preserve the complete existing content-boundary verification.

Constraints.Constraint: Write scope is exactly these six paths: mark-quicklook/Sources/PreviewExtension/Resources/github-dark.css, tests/quicklook/PreviewBoundaryTests.swift, tools/check-quicklook.mjs, tests/renderer/quicklook-runner.test.js, .grace/graph/features.xml, .grace/verification/features.xml. The following remain byte-identical to the verified current baseline: mark-quicklook/Sources/Shared/MarkdownRenderer.swift, mark-quicklook/Sources/PreviewExtension/PreviewProvider.swift, mark-quicklook/Sources/PreviewExtension/Resources/style.css, mark-quicklook/Sources/PreviewExtension/Resources/markdown-it.min.js, mark-quicklook/Sources/PreviewExtension/Resources/highlight.min.js, and MarkPreview.entitlements.

Append only prefers-color-scheme: light color/background overrides to the end of the existing github-dark.css resource. Retain its resource name, bundle load order, attribution header and every dark/default declaration. No new runtime resource, downloaded asset, dependency, theme engine or project-file change.

Select the existing nested hljs spans even though the code root carries only language-* classes; do not add an .hljs root, override markdown-it/highlight markup, or introduce a script or theme bridge to compensate for absent root classes.

Change only foreground/background colors inside the new light branch. Do not alter font family, size, weight, style, spacing, padding, borders, scroll behavior, code-block geometry, Markdown parsing, language detection, body text, document CSS variables or emphasis/strong/section typography; only their light foregrounds change.

Preserve the accepted QuickLook hardening boundary unchanged: per-render nonce CSP (default-src 'none', nonce-gated scripts, style-src 'unsafe-inline' solely for markdown-it's controlled table-cell alignment, img-src data:, connect-src/frame-src/object-src/form-action/base-uri 'none'), base64 document data embedding, raw HTML disabled, escaped titles, selected-file read scope, ephemeral WKWebView data store, about:blank-only navigation and new-window denial, embedded-raster-only image policy, absent network-client entitlement. No security relaxation for palette verification; no network access is introduced.

The light palette is the proposed local adaptation of the incumbent GitHub-inspired system: upstream highlight.js 11.9.0 GitHub Light color roles plus locally darker variants where upstream values fall below 4.5:1 on the existing #f6f8fa pre background. Groups and values: base #1f2328; keyword #cf222e; title #6f42c1; constant #005cc5; string #032f62; builtin #953800; comment #656d76; tag #116329; inherited-emphasis #1f2328; section #005cc5; bullet #735c0f — all on the existing light pre background #f6f8fa; addition #116329 on #f0fff4; deletion #b31d28 on #ffeef0. Comment/base reuse existing QuickLook light tones. This is an adaptation, not a reproduction of GitHub site CSS or a full upstream stylesheet copy.

Keep dark/default computed colors and syntax output unchanged; an environment matching neither explicit scheme retains the existing default dark palette. A supported appearance switch updates colors without reloading, re-rendering or changing code text.

Extend the existing owned native fixture and required-case protocol with theme-light and theme-dark cases under both engines' coverage; all existing 24 named boundary cases remain mandatory and unchanged. Missing, duplicate, failed or absent native theme evidence is runner failure, never a skip or an empty pass; no unsupported-host success path is added.

Native theme fixtures may set appearance only on their own provider/view/window. Do not switch system appearance, install or register a host/extension, change file associations, touch owner documents or launch the owner-installed Mark. Use unsigned isolated artifacts with fixed identifiers and remove them after the run.

A browser screenshot/computed-style run is visual evidence only, not PreviewProvider/WKWebView acceptance; a Foundation-only HTML generator proves Swift output provenance, not native extension acceptance. Installed Finder/owner/platform acceptance remains separately identified until evidence or an explicit owner exception exists.

Execute sequentially against the current graph. Preserve M-073/V-M-073 ownership and all existing tests, runner deadlines and safety assertions; do not add retries or skips, weaken floors, change production signing, versions, entitlements or frozen archived bundles. The hosted quicklook-native job (M-046-owned) keeps its required-gate role; extending its fixture cases must not weaken its inverses or budgets.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No preview redesign, light/dark mode selector, sync with all Mark document themes, new syntax engine or languages, theme preferences/events, or full accessibility audit.

No HTML, CSP, resource, transport or navigation policy change; no app-wide theme migration or product-wide design-system introduction. The existing QuickLook CSS and packaged appearance remain the visual authority for this bounded correction.
No release, tag, version change, production signing, installation or LaunchServices registration, workflow dispatch, App Store upload or owner-application mutation is authorized by this change.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first evidence on the unchanged sources reproduces the light-token contrast failure, then passes after the resource override. Evidence uses the real renderer and packaged resources with a known-language JavaScript block, a Python block and an unknown-language/plain plus inline controls, preserving exact rendered text, token classes and code geometry.

All 41 existing color-bearing selectors are covered by the 13 light palette groups with deterministic selector and contrast checks against the actually applicable background. Representative markdown-generated tokens are measured in the actual rendered document; any supplemental controlled selector spans are labelled separately from real Markdown/highlight cases. Addition/deletion are measured against their own token backgrounds.

Chromium and WebKit render actual Swift HTML in light and dark, capturing readable code and page-context screenshots. Light values follow the specified palette, all light target ratios reach 4.5:1 before rounding, plain/inline controls stay readable, no page errors or external resource requests occur, and switching appearance preserves content and geometry.

The actual native PreviewProvider/WKWebView fixture proves light and dark media matches, computed syntax colors and contrast without system appearance changes. Both new theme cases are required elements of the native result protocol; a failed, missing or duplicated theme result fails runner validation. The complete previous 24-case security matrix and the independent zero-observer-request validation remain intact.

All dark/default rules retain their original declarations and visual values, and the byte-identical file set is proven unchanged against the plan's recorded digests; only light color/background declarations affect the preview.

The existing runner unit suite plus new completeness/failure controls, the actual native boundary and theme checks, the unsigned MarkPreview extension build, GRACE current/target/final gates and normal commit/push/review and exact-head hosted checks pass for the final candidate. Unavailable native evidence is classified honestly; source or browser success never bypasses a native gate.

M-073/V-M-073 and the M-046 quicklook-native job ownership markup in .grace/graph/features.xml and .grace/verification/features.xml describe the theme evidence and its limits while retaining security ownership. Apply/archive and train admission follow their normal separate decisions; owner/platform acceptance and release authorization remain separate.

All task-owned fixture and browser processes are closed and reaped, owned app/binary/packaged artifacts are removed after shutdown, and source, recipe, hash, log, HTML and screenshot evidence is retained. Toolchain caches and owner state are preserved.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: xcodebuild -project mark-quicklook/MarkQuickLook.xcodeproj -target MarkPreview -configuration Debug SYMROOT="$PWD/.claude/quicklook-content-boundary/target-build/products" OBJROOT="$PWD/.claude/quicklook-content-boundary/target-build/intermediates" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY= REGISTER_APP_WITH_LAUNCH_SERVICES=NO SKIP_INSTALL=YES build
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The QuickLook native boundary job's fixture suite (the hosted macos-15 quicklook-native job and its local equivalent) must include the new theme-light/theme-dark cases under the unchanged fail-closed result protocol: complete native result set, successful native process, independent zero observer requests, the previous 24 named security cases, unchanged-source and dark-rule assertions, and the unsigned extension build. An approved sequential plan binds the exact media/contrast assertions, actual Swift HTML provenance, browser screenshot matrix, gate budgets and evidence retention before approval.

The plan must name exact commands and record baseline digests of the byte-identical file set on the fresh head before implementation; historical review baselines are not re-measured as current evidence.

Assumptions.Assumption: The owner approves the bounded light palette, the 4.5:1 unrounded contrast target and the CSS-only approach as part of turning this draft into an approved spec. Writing the draft approves no plan, implementation, apply/archive, installation or release.

Existing mode behavior and the packaged QuickLook visual identity remain authoritative; the absence of product-wide DESIGN.md is not a reason to introduce a separate design system or expand this correction.
